findings.claim: The two-line [ACDSL-PROJECTION] header (lines 2-3) is committed into HEAD even though its own text reads 'working-copy view, stripped before commit'. No other routine script carries it: git show HEAD:routines/{skill-eval,smine-nightly,coverage-increaser}/run.sh all begin '#!/usr/bin/env bash' followed directly by a normal description comment, and this header was added in this very range (git diff a7abd0..HEAD shows the two lines as + additions in the committed tree). Concrete trigger: reading the committed file shows a projection header every sibling routine/*/run.sh lacks and that contradicts its own strip-before-commit contract — it does not read like the repo wrote it.
findings.fix: Strip lines 2-3 (the '# [ACDSL-PROJECTION]' header and its rule line) from the committed file, matching every other routines/*/run.sh; the projection is a working-copy overlay, not committed content.
findings.evidence: Re-read run.sh:1-3 in full; text is '# [ACDSL-PROJECTION] 1 rule(s) govern this file — working-copy view, stripped before commit'. Confirmed via git show HEAD:routines/skill-eval/run.sh, routines/smine-nightly/run.sh, routines/coverage-increaser/run.sh — none carry a projection header (all start shebang + plain comment). Grep 'ACDSL-PROJECTION' over routines/**/*.sh matches only this file. git diff a7abd0..HEAD shows the two header lines added as committed additions.

findings.claim: 'done < <(cat "$cells_file")' is a useless use of cat inside a process substitution; the while-read loop can read the file directly. The repo's own cell-pattern source it mirrors, routines/_lib/matrix.sh:226, uses the direct form 'done < "$plan"'. Concrete: the redirect spawns a needless cat subprocess and diverges from the sibling idiom.
findings.evidence: Re-read run.sh:263-294 (the mechanical-trace while loop) — the loop only reads, never needs cat. Confirmed matrix.sh:211-226 uses 'done < "$plan"' / 'done <<< "$files"' directly; grep 'done < <(cat ' over *.sh matches only run.sh:294.

findings.claim: Variable 'total_major' (assigned lines 227-232, printed line 233) counts pre-dedup candidates at/above the configured '$refute_rank' threshold, which derives from ROUTINE_REFUTE_LEVEL (blocker|major|minor|nit|info) — not specifically 'major'. With ROUTINE_REFUTE_LEVEL=blocker the variable holds the blocker count yet the name and the message 'refute: N candidate(s) at threshold $refute_level (of $total_major pre-dedup...)' label it 'major', misleading a reader who set a non-major threshold.
findings.fix: Rename to a threshold-generic name such as 'total_at_threshold' or 'candidates_predical' (both assignment sites and the echo on line 233).
findings.evidence: Re-read run.sh:34 (refute_level default), 39-47 (refute_rank mapping over all five levels + none), 227-233. The jq select uses '>= $thr' where $thr=$refute_rank, so the count tracks the configured level; the name hardcodes 'major', accurate only for the default. Message string on line 233 confirmed.
